what_it_does: Bugs in programs that use multiple threads (concurrent programs) are notoriously hard to find because they only appear when threads happen to run in a specific order — one thread reads a value just before another writes it, for example. Testing tools try to explore many different orderings, but existing random testing methods are biased: they over-sample some orderings and almost never visit others, so rare bugs stay hidden. SURW (Selectively Uniform Random Walk) fixes this by carefully choosing which program events to include in the sampling and then sampling those orderings uniformly — every ordering gets an equal chance of being tested. This is done without needing deep knowledge of the program's internals.
